rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Traced every pronoun/demonstrative under sequential read. Chunk 0 line 5 'it runs...it has...it has' -> 'the Lemmings game' named line 5's own opening clause, in-sentence. Chunk 1 line 10 'in it' -> 'a new folder' same bullet; line 11 'that folder' -> line 10's folder, in-chunk. Chunk 1 line 13 'Open the page' -> 'a single browser page' line 12, in-chunk. Chunk 2 line 17 'the game' and line 18 'the repo' both reuse chunk-0/chunk-1 nouns (Lemmings game line 5, git repo line 10) across slides -- explicitly protected under the rule's own carve-out ('a term introduced on an earlier slide and reused... FINE'). Chunk 2 line 19 'Before you close the session' -> 'a Claude Code session' line 11, immediate-continuation reuse, also fine. Chunk 2 line 19's flag-block sentences name 'Module 3' directly (not a pronoun) and, in the no-module branch, 'the later task sizes' -- an explicitly-flagged forward mention ('later'), not a bare unresolved pronoun; both branches resolve one slide ahead at chunk 3's own header. Chunk 4 line 32 'The running game, the test suite, the commit history, and the one bug' resolve to chunk 1 line 12 (game), chunk 2 line 17 (test suite), chunk 2 line 18 (commit history), chunk 1 line 13 (the bug). No never-named or stranded referent anywhere.

Exactly two cross-document references in the body. Chunk 3 line 23: '[prework](../prework.md)' -- named by link text, no page-position language. Chunk 2 line 19 flag:module branch: 'Module 3' -- named by its stable module number, the same convention this file itself uses for its own module ('your Module 1 material' line 9, 'your Module 1 bug' line 13, '## Bring to Module 1' line 30), not a positional locator ('two modules from now'). Neither points at a sibling file by page position.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim: chunk 1 = the build steps to a running game; chunk 2 = leave the session with tests, commit history, and a data-touching feature; chunk 3 = the four task sizes, fully enumerated in-chunk; chunk 4 = the four things to bring, one complete sentence. No chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment.

Chunk 1 'Get to a running game' -> content is exactly the steps to a first playable build, ending at 'Open the page and play' (line 13). Chunk 2 'Leave it with tests and a data surface' -> content is exactly tests (line 17), commit history (line 18), and a data-touching feature (line 19) -- both header nouns ('tests', 'data surface') land, regardless of which flag branch renders. Chunk 3 'Where the four task sizes come from' -> content is exactly the four task-size definitions. Chunk 4 'Bring to Module 1' -> content is exactly the bring-list. No header promises content the chunk doesn't deliver.

Checked every chunk against all six sub-items. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triple. `grep -inE 'one of the most|best|incredibly|truly|really'` over the body -> 0 hits, no self-grading superlative. No number-stated-then-retracted pattern (the two numeric mentions -- 'two levels', 'three lemming actions' -- are plain unretracted specs). No abstraction-noun stack ('data surface' and 'surface area' are concrete domain terms tied to a named mechanism, not free-floating abstractions). No verb triplet with an empty leg. Body reads as plain instructional prose throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -inE 'surface|beat|mood|compendium|forcing function|\bfiring\b'` over the body -> 4 hits, all 'surface': line 12 'surface area' (ordinary engineering usage, code with room to grow); header line 15 'data surface', line 19 (both flag branches) 'That surface'/'one kind of surface'. Weighed deliberately: the repo's own internal dialect sense of 'surface' is the editorial/writing-surface metaphor (this very compendium's vocabulary); the sense used here is 'attack surface'/'data surface', standard security-engineering terminology tied explicitly in the same sentence to access control and STRIDE -- the exact vocabulary Module 3 teaches. An AE101 engineer reads this as domain jargon they already half-know, not repo-internal shorthand. No 'beat', 'mood', 'compendium', 'forcing function', or bare 'firing' anywhere in the body.

No other bold anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 2, line 19, flag:module:earn-the-trust branch, first sentence: 'That surface is what Module 3 reads when you map access control and run STRIDE against it.' Subject test passes ('That surface' = the student's own planted artifact) but the predicate promises what a LATER MODULE does with it ('Module 3 reads... you map access control and run STRIDE') -- the slides-class instantiation of check_student_facing.md §33's predicate-leak clause that this rule's (b) sub-class explicitly cross-references, same shape as the compendium's own worked example ('un-packaged first is by design'). Deletion test: cut the sentence and read the bullet's neighbours -- 'ask Claude to add one feature that touches data or other players: a shareable level via a URL, a score you submit, or saved progress. A toy game with no data has nothing to threat-model.' The instruction stays fully actionable and the second sentence alone still supplies the in-the-moment rationale (why a data-touching feature, not why THIS specific module reads it later); the cut sentence's distinct contribution is only the cross-module promise. Checked the maintainer block for a covering accept-note first (lines 34-82): none of the four dated notes attests this specific sentence. The sibling no-module:earn-the-trust branch ('...the later task sizes want somewhere real to land') was also checked and does NOT trip this rule -- it forward-points to this SAME file's own next chunk (chunk 3, one slide ahead), not to another module's activity, so it stays same-document connective tissue rather than cross-module cartography. Harm: low -- the flag:module branch's instruction is still fully followable without the cut sentence, this is a 'could be tighter' cost, not a comprehension failure, which is why it is filed non-blocking.
